title: Meet G, H and I
goal: Recognise, name and write G, H, I.
cue: A letter has a name. Later, we will learn the sounds it can represent in words. Today, say the letter names.
spelling: A letter has a name. Later, we will learn the sounds it can represent in words. Today, say the letter names.
task: Point to G and I. Say their names, then write their lowercase partners.
story: The letter G has a big form and a small form.
reviewPrompt: Recall two letters from day 2 before looking back.

cards.title: Letter G
sections: goat /ɡoʊt/ · an animal often kept on a farm
In goat, g represents /ɡ/. This is a word sound, not the letter name.
Write G and g three times. Cover the model and write the pair again.

articulation.label: Letter H
articulation.alt: Letter H: /eɪ/ → /tʃ/. Tongue, lips, contact and airflow positions.
notes: /ɪ/: Raise the front tongue; narrow the jaw gap.
/tʃ/: Brief closure, then a narrow sh-like release.
articulation.note: Keep each vowel glide inside one syllable.

articulation.label: Letter I
articulation.alt: Letter I: /aɪ/. Tongue, lips, contact and airflow positions.
notes: /a/: Start with the tongue low and jaw open.
/ɪ/: Glide up and forward; narrow the jaw gap.
articulation.note: Keep each vowel glide inside one syllable.

cards.title: Five words to hear and use
sections: an animal often kept on a farm. The goat eats grass.
a covering worn on the head. Mia takes her coat and hat.
The colored liquid used in some pens. This pen has blue ink.
the part at the end of your arm with fingers. Mia points to her right hand.
an adult female chicken. The hen has three eggs.
Listen to each word. Point or act to show its meaning. Say one word, then one short sentence. Ask for help with spelling patterns you have not learned yet.
